### Observed differences

- Activity A01 was not observed in any of the 200 earlier traces (0% participation, mean 0 occurrences per trace). In the later window it appears in about 31 of 200 traces (roughly 15%), averages about 0.29 occurrences per trace, and occurs more than once in a trace in about 8% of traces. [OCC001]
- In the later window, A01's outgoing transitions split between two successors: about 54% go to A09 and about 46% to A10 (based on 57 observed outgoing transitions). In the earlier window no outgoing transitions of A01 were observed, because A01 itself was not observed. [DIR001]
- In the later window, A01 occurs on average at about two-thirds of the trace's event positions (median about 0.70; the middle half of its occurrences fall between roughly 0.51 and 0.88). No positional observations exist for the earlier window. These are event-order positions, not clock times. [POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 appears as a step in the later window that was not observed before: it runs in roughly 15% of later traces, is occasionally repeated within a trace, sits around two-thirds of the way through the trace by event order, and is followed by either A09 (about 54% of its outgoing transitions) or A10 (about 46%). [OCC001, DIR001, POS001]

Supporting signs: all three qualified items concern A01 and agree in direction; the screening produced 3 items where only about 0.17 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the set is unlikely to be a chance product; and each item's difference exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled traces. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window only establishes that A01 was not observed there, so the evidence cannot distinguish a genuinely new step from a previously very rare step that went unobserved; the three items describe the same traces and are therefore not independent confirmations; and nothing in the evidence shows what precedes A01 or why it occurs in only part of the later traces. The main competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is that A01 existed earlier at a much lower rate and simply did not appear in the 200 earlier traces. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001]

Let me analyse this evidence.

Screening: 34 units tested, 3 items qualified, 0.17 expected without change. 3 items is many times larger than 0.17 (about 18x). So the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past the screening comparison.

The evidence: three items, all about activity A01.

OCC001: A01 occurrences. Before: mean 0.0 per trace, participation 0.0, recurrence 0.0. After: mean 0.285 per trace, participation 0.155 (about 31 in 200 traces), recurrence 0.08. So A01 was absent in the before window and appears in the after window in about 15-16% of traces, sometimes repeated (recurrence support 0.08, so about 16 of 200 traces have it more than once? Actually recurrence support 0.08 means 8% of traces have it repeated). Support: before 0, after 31.

DIR001: outgoing transitions of A01. Before: empty profile (no observations). After: A09 gets ~54%, A10 ~46% of outgoing transitions. Support before 0, after 57 (57 outgoing transitions observed across traces containing A01).

POS001: position of A01. Before: no support. After: support 0.155, mean position ~0.66 of the trace, median ~0.70, q25 ~0.51, q75 ~0.875. So A01 occurs around two-thirds into the trace when it appears.

So the behaviour: A01 was not observed at all in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces), and in the later window it appears in about 31 of 200 traces (~15%), sometimes more than once per trace (about 16 of 200 traces, recurrence 8%), typically around position 0.66-0.70 of the trace, and when it occurs it is followed by A09 (about 54% of its outgoing transitions) or A10 (about 46%).

This is an activity that appears (is added / becomes present) in the later window. This is not a shift in path frequencies between existing alternatives — A01 is absent in one window, so it's an addition/becoming optional. The hypothesis: A01 was added to the process (or became observable) in the later window, inserted in the later part of traces, followed by either A09 or A10.

Support level: The screening comparison: 3 items vs 0.17 expected — many times larger, so chance as a whole can't explain it. Then judge by directness, consistency, ability to rule out competing explanations. All three items concern A01 and agree: it went from absent to present, with consistent directional and positional profiles. The evidence directly shows appearance of a new activity. However, one caveat: zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window. With 200 traces in the before window and 0 observations, if the activity occurred at a rate similar to the after window (~15% participation), the probability of observing zero in 200 traces is essentially nil — but the instructions say "Zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window." So we should phrase carefully: A01 was not observed in the earlier window.

Is this "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence is direct (OCC, DIR, POS all about A01), consistent (all three agree), and the item count is many times the chance expectation. The hypothesis: A01 was introduced/appears in the later window, occurring in roughly the later-middle portion of traces, followed by A09 or A10. Competing explanation: A01 existed before but was not observed in the before sample (rare variant / sampling) — though with 200 traces and 0 occurrences, that's unlikely if its rate were similar; but the instructions say zero participation only means not observed. Also, the before window has zero support for DIR and POS, so we cannot say anything about where A01 sat before — but since it wasn't observed at all, the hypothesis is about appearance.

I think "Supported hypothesis" is appropriate: direct, consistent, three agreeing items, count far above chance expectation. The main limitation: we cannot tell from this evidence whether A01 was truly absent before or merely too rare to be observed; also we don't know what precedes A01 (only successors via DIR).

Actually, let me reconsider: is this a "change in structure"? The hypothesis categories: participation changes support hypotheses that part of the process is executed more often, skipped, etc. Zero participation means not observed. The appearance of an activity in one window only — the guidance about "a rare variant can appear in one window only" is a caution. But here the screening count (3 vs 0.17) plus the consistency across three indicators (occurrence, direction, position) all pointing to the same new activity supports a real change. The empirical strength ~0.995 for each.

Hmm, but the caution: "A count of the same order as that expectation ... choose Insufficient evidence". 3 vs 0.17 is ~18x, many times larger. So we proceed.

Directness: OCC shows appearance; DIR shows its outgoing edges (new relational info); POS shows placement. All directly about A01. Consistency: all agree. Competing explanations: sampling (A01 present but unobserved before) — with 0/200 before vs 31/200 after, if the underlying rate were ~15% in both windows, zero in 200 is essentially impossible; but strictly, the evidence can't fully rule out that A01 was extremely rare before. Also we can't tell what triggers A01 or what precedes it.

I'd say Supported hypothesis: "A01 appears in the later window" — an activity addition / becoming present. State as possibility supported by evidence.

Now the writing rules:

- Every bullet/paragraph stating a fact about data or hypothesis must end with exactly one pair of square brackets listing evidence ids.
- Use rounded percentages or fractions: "about 31 in 200 traces (roughly 15%)".
- Describe before and after for each difference.
- Don't speculate about causes.
- No time/resource items (no TWAIT, ASSIGN, CONC, HAND), so don't discuss time or resources. POS uses event positions — note that position is by event order, not clock time; I should be careful: "POS and LAG use event positions, not clock time. A position shift alone does not show that an activity was moved." Here POS is used to describe where A01 sits in the later window, not to claim a move. That's fine as description.

Hmm, "why it occurs in only part of the traces" — that's fine as limitation. Also competing explanation: sampling. I mentioned it in limitations. The instruction says "Briefly mention an important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out." Good.
